voc-3.title: Spellings and Commonly Confused Words
voc-3.notes:
Correct spelling and choosing the right word from commonly confused pairs are directly tested in NEA. Many English words are confused because they sound similar (homophones) or are spelled similarly.

COMMONLY CONFUSED WORDS (HOMOPHONES AND NEAR-HOMOPHONES):

Accept / Except:
Accept = to receive/agree to. He accepted the award.
Except = excluding. Everyone came except him.

Affect / Effect:
Affect = verb (to influence). The weather affected the match.
Effect = noun (result). The effect was devastating. (Exception: 'to effect change' = rare verb form)

Advice / Advise:
Advice = noun (uncountable). Take my advice.
Advise = verb. I advise you to study hard.

Allusion / Illusion:
Allusion = indirect reference. He made an allusion to the war.
Illusion = false impression. It was just an illusion.

Altitude / Attitude:
Altitude = height above sea level.
Attitude = one's mental stance or opinion.

Assent / Ascent:
Assent = agreement. She gave her assent.
Ascent = going up. The ascent of the mountain was difficult.

Complement / Compliment:
Complement = something that completes/enhances. The sauce complements the dish.
Compliment = praise. He paid her a compliment.

Council / Counsel:
Council = a governing body. The town council met.
Counsel = advice or a lawyer. He sought legal counsel.

Emigrate / Immigrate:
Emigrate = to leave your country. He emigrated from India.
Immigrate = to enter a new country. She immigrated to Canada.

Principal / Principle:
Principal = head/main. The school principal. The principal reason.
Principle = a rule or belief. A man of principles.

Stationary / Stationery:
Stationary = not moving. The vehicle was stationary.
Stationery = writing materials (paper, pens). Buy stationery from the shop.

Than / Then:
Than = comparison. She is taller than me.
Then = time/sequence. First study, then relax.

There / Their / They're:
There = place. Go there.
Their = possessive. Their ship. 
They're = they are. They're ready.

COMMON SPELLING ERRORS:
accomodation ✗ → accommodation ✓
occasion ✓ (two c's, one s)
neccessary ✗ → necessary ✓
recommend ✓ (one c, two m's)
calender ✗ → calendar ✓
reiceve ✗ → receive ✓ (i before e except after c)
difinitely ✗ → definitely ✓
grammer ✗ → grammar ✓
points: Accept = receive/agree; Except = excluding/other than.
Affect = verb (influence); Effect = noun (result).
Advice = noun; Advise = verb.
Complement = completes/enhances; Compliment = praise.
Principal = head/main; Principle = rule/belief.
Stationary = not moving; Stationery = writing materials (e for envelopes).
Emigrate = leave a country; Immigrate = enter a new country.
There = place; Their = possession; They're = they are.
Spelling rule: i before e except after c (receive, ceiling, deceive).
Accommodation: two c's, two m's; Necessary: one c, one s; Recommend: one c, two m's.
examples: Confused words: 'The principal principle of the school is honesty.'
Confused words: 'The car remained stationary while I bought stationery.'
Spelling: 'I definitely recommend this accommodation.'
Confused words: 'His positive attitude affected everyone; the effect was remarkable.'
Homophones: 'They're going to their base over there.'
voc-3.summary: Commonly confused words must be memorised by meaning: accept/except, affect/effect, advice/advise, complement/compliment, principal/principle, stationary/stationery, emigrate/immigrate, council/counsel. Spelling rules: i before e except after c (receive), accommodation (2c,2m), necessary (1c,1s), recommend (1c,2m), definitely (not 'difinitely'), grammar (not 'grammer'). There/Their/They're is a very common exam trap.

ic-3.title: Executive, Legislature and Judiciary in India
ic-3.notes:
India's democratic government is divided into three branches that work independently yet are interconnected: the Legislature (makes laws), the Executive (implements laws), and the Judiciary (interprets laws and ensures justice).

THE LEGISLATURE:
The Parliament of India is bicameral — it has two houses.

Lok Sabha (House of the People):
— Lower house; directly elected by the people.
— Maximum strength: 552 (543 elected + 2 Anglo-Indian nominated — nomination abolished in 2020 by 104th Amendment).
— Term: 5 years. Can be dissolved by President on advice of PM.
— Minimum age: 25 years to contest.
— Money Bills originate only in Lok Sabha.
— Presided over by the Speaker.

Rajya Sabha (Council of States):
— Upper house; indirectly elected by State Legislative Assemblies.
— Maximum strength: 250 (238 elected from states + 12 nominated by President for expertise in arts, literature, science, social service).
— Permanent body — cannot be dissolved. 1/3 members retire every 2 years.
— Term of each member: 6 years. Minimum age: 30 years.
— Presided over by the Vice President (ex-officio Chairman).

THE EXECUTIVE:
The President of India: Constitutional head. Nominal executive. Powers exercised on advice of the Council of Ministers headed by PM. Elected indirectly by elected MPs and MLAs.

The Prime Minister: Real executive head. Leader of the majority party in Lok Sabha. Heads the Cabinet. Advises the President.

The Council of Ministers: Collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.

THE JUDICIARY:
Supreme Court: Apex court of India. Chief Justice of India + maximum 33 other judges. Appointed by President. Original jurisdiction, appellate jurisdiction, advisory jurisdiction.
High Court: Each state has a High Court. Appellate court for the state.
District Courts: Trial courts at district level.
Doctrine of Judicial Review: Courts can declare laws unconstitutional if they violate the Constitution.
points: Parliament is bicameral: Lok Sabha (lower) and Rajya Sabha (upper).
Lok Sabha: 543 elected seats, 5-year term, minimum age 25, presided by Speaker.
Rajya Sabha: 250 seats, permanent body, 6-year terms, minimum age 30, VP is Chairman.
Money Bills originate only in Lok Sabha — Rajya Sabha cannot amend them.
President = nominal/constitutional executive. PM = real executive head.
Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to Lok Sabha.
Supreme Court has original, appellate, and advisory jurisdiction.
Chief Justice of India heads the Supreme Court (max 34 judges including CJI).
Judicial review: courts can declare laws unconstitutional.
High Courts head state judiciary; District Courts handle trials at district level.
examples: Money Bills: Budget (Union Budget) can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha.
Rajya Sabha permanence: even if PM resigns and Lok Sabha dissolves, Rajya Sabha continues.
Judicial review: Supreme Court struck down NJAC Act (2015) as unconstitutional.
President's appointment: elected by MPs and MLAs, not directly by people.
Speaker's role: presides over Lok Sabha, maintains order, decides on Money Bills.
ic-3.summary: India's government has three branches. Legislature: Parliament = Lok Sabha (543 elected, 5-year term, Speaker) + Rajya Sabha (250 seats, permanent, VP as Chairman). Executive: President (nominal head) + PM (real head) + Council of Ministers. Judiciary: Supreme Court (CJI + 33 judges, highest court) → High Courts → District Courts. Money Bills originate only in Lok Sabha. Judicial review lets courts declare laws unconstitutional.

questions.explanation: Money Bills can only be introduced in Lok Sabha. Rajya Sabha can only make recommendations, not amend them.

questions.explanation: The Prime Minister is the real executive head. The President is the constitutional/nominal head.

questions.question: The Rajya Sabha is a permanent body because:
questions.explanation: Rajya Sabha cannot be dissolved — only 1/3 of its members retire every 2 years, making it a continuing chamber.

questions.question: The Supreme Court of India has how many judges (maximum, including CJI)?
questions.explanation: The Supreme Court can have a maximum of 34 judges: the Chief Justice + 33 other judges.

questions.question: The doctrine of Judicial Review means:
options: Courts review the performance of ministers
Courts advise the Parliament on laws
questions.explanation: Judicial Review is the power of the Supreme Court to strike down any law that violates the Constitution.

questions.question: The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to:
questions.explanation: The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha — they must maintain its confidence.

questions.question: 12 members of Rajya Sabha are nominated by the President for their expertise in:
questions.explanation: The President nominates 12 members to Rajya Sabha who have distinguished themselves in arts, literature, science, or social service.

questions.question: The Speaker of Lok Sabha is elected by:
questions.explanation: The Speaker of Lok Sabha is elected by the members of Lok Sabha from among themselves.

questions.question: Term of each Rajya Sabha member is:
questions.explanation: Each Rajya Sabha member has a term of 6 years, but 1/3 retire every 2 years.

questions.question: High Courts in India have jurisdiction over:
options: The respective state and its courts
questions.explanation: Each High Court has jurisdiction over its state and supervises all subordinate courts within that state.

questions.question: The President of India is elected by:
options: Elected members of Parliament and State Assemblies
questions.explanation: The President is elected by an Electoral College consisting of elected members of both Houses of Parliament and State Legislative Assemblies.

ic-4.title: Federalism and Local Governments in India
ic-4.notes:
Federalism is a system of government where power is divided between the central (national) government and the state governments. India has a federal structure with a strong unitary bias.

INDIAN FEDERALISM:
India is a 'Union of States' (not a 'Federation of States') — as stated in Article 1 of the Constitution. This means states cannot secede from India, unlike in a pure federation.

DIVISION OF POWERS — THREE LISTS:
The Seventh Schedule of the Constitution divides legislative powers:

1. UNION LIST: Subjects on which only Parliament can legislate. 100 subjects. Examples: Defence, Foreign affairs, Currency, Banking, Railways, Atomic energy, Census.

2. STATE LIST: Subjects on which only State Legislatures can legislate. 61 subjects. Examples: Police, Public order, Agriculture, Land, Local government, Prisons.

3. CONCURRENT LIST: Both Parliament and State Legislatures can legislate. 52 subjects. In case of conflict, Central law prevails. Examples: Education, Marriage, Forests, Trade unions, Criminal law.

RESIDUARY POWERS: Subjects not in any list go to Parliament (unlike in some federations where they go to states).

CENTRAL DOMINANCE: India's federalism has strong central features — Governor appointed by Centre, Emergency provisions (Articles 352, 356, 360), Single citizenship, Integrated judiciary, All-India Services (IAS, IPS, IFS).

73rd AND 74th CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENTS (1992):
These amendments established Local Self Government.
73rd Amendment — Panchayati Raj (rural):
— Three-tier system: Gram Panchayat → Panchayat Samiti → Zila Parishad.
— Reservation for SC, ST, and women (1/3 seats).
— State Finance Commission, State Election Commission mandated.
— Elections every 5 years.

74th Amendment — Urban Local Bodies (ULBs):
— Municipal Corporations (large cities), Municipal Councils, Nagar Panchayats (transitional areas).
— Reservation for SC, ST, women.
— Mayor heads Municipal Corporation.
points: India is a 'Union of States' — states cannot secede. Strongly federal with unitary bias.
Seventh Schedule: Union List (Parliament only), State List (States only), Concurrent List (both).
Union List: ~100 subjects — defence, currency, banking, railways, foreign affairs.
State List: ~61 subjects — police, agriculture, land, public order.
Concurrent List: ~52 subjects — education, marriage, forests. Centre prevails in conflict.
Residuary powers go to Parliament (Centre), not states.
73rd Amendment (1992): Panchayati Raj — 3 tiers: Gram Panchayat, Panchayat Samiti, Zila Parishad.
74th Amendment (1992): Urban Local Bodies — Municipal Corporations, Councils, Nagar Panchayats.
Reservation: SC, ST, and minimum 1/3 women in both Panchayati Raj and ULBs.
State Election Commission conducts elections to local bodies every 5 years.
examples: Union List: Parliament passes laws on defence — states cannot pass conflicting laws.
Concurrent List: Both Centre and states can legislate on Education; if conflict, Central law prevails.
73rd Amendment: A Gram Panchayat at village level manages local development, roads, water.
74th Amendment: Delhi Municipal Corporation (DMC) is a Municipal Corporation under 74th Amendment.
Residuary power: Cyber law (not in any list when drafted) — Parliament legislates via residuary powers.
ic-4.summary: India is a Union of States with federal structure and strong central bias. Seventh Schedule divides powers: Union List (Centre only — defence, currency), State List (states only — police, land), Concurrent List (both — education, forests; Centre prevails in conflict). Residuary powers go to Centre. 73rd Amendment created 3-tier Panchayati Raj (village-block-district). 74th Amendment created Urban Local Bodies. Both mandate reservations for SC, ST, and women (1/3 minimum).

questions.question: India is constitutionally described as:
questions.explanation: Article 1 of the Indian Constitution describes India as a 'Union of States', emphasising that states cannot secede.

questions.question: Subjects on which only Parliament can legislate are in the:
questions.explanation: The Union List contains subjects exclusively under Parliament's legislative power (e.g., defence, banking, railways).

questions.question: In case of conflict between Central and State laws on a Concurrent List subject:
options: The matter goes to Supreme Court
questions.explanation: Article 254: If there is a conflict between Central and State laws on a Concurrent List subject, the Central law prevails.

questions.question: Residuary powers in India vest in:
questions.explanation: Residuary powers — topics not in any list — are given to Parliament (Centre), unlike in some federations.

questions.question: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment (1992) relates to:
questions.explanation: The 73rd Amendment gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj — the 3-tier system of rural self-government.

questions.question: The three tiers of Panchayati Raj are:
options: Gram Panchayat, Panchayat Samiti, Zila Parishad
questions.explanation: The three tiers: Gram Panchayat (village), Panchayat Samiti (block), Zila Parishad (district).

questions.question: The 74th Constitutional Amendment relates to:
questions.explanation: The 74th Amendment gave constitutional status to Urban Local Bodies — Municipal Corporations, Councils, Nagar Panchayats.

questions.question: Which is NOT in the State List?
questions.explanation: 'Currency' is in the Union List — only Parliament can make laws on it. Police, Agriculture, and Public order are in the State List.

questions.question: The minimum reservation for women in Panchayati Raj institutions is:
questions.explanation: The 73rd Amendment mandates minimum 1/3 (33%) reservation for women in Panchayati Raj institutions. Several states have increased it to 50%.

questions.question: Education is in which list?
questions.explanation: Education was moved to the Concurrent List by the 42nd Amendment (1976) — both Centre and states can legislate on it.

questions.question: Which body conducts elections to Panchayati Raj institutions?
questions.explanation: The State Election Commission conducts elections to Panchayati Raj and Urban Local Body institutions in each state.

questions.question: The Governor of a state is appointed by:
questions.explanation: The Governor is appointed by the President of India on the advice of the Prime Minister — this shows India's unitary bias.

questions.question: Which is an example of a Union List subject?
questions.explanation: Atomic energy is in the Union List — only Parliament can legislate on it. It is a sensitive national security subject.

questions.question: The head of a Municipal Corporation is called:
questions.explanation: The Mayor is the head of a Municipal Corporation. Sarpanch heads a Gram Panchayat.

questions.question: India's federalism is described as having 'unitary bias' because:
options: Centre has more powers than states in several aspects
questions.explanation: India's federalism has unitary features: single citizenship, Governor appointed by Centre, Emergency provisions, residuary powers with Centre, strong All-India Services.

ag-1.title: Grammatical Structures in Meaningful Contexts
ag-1.notes:
Grammar is the set of rules that governs how words combine to form sentences. Understanding grammatical structures in context — not in isolation — is the key skill tested in NEA.

PARTS OF SPEECH (8 types):
1. NOUN: Names a person, place, thing, or idea. Types: Proper (India, Rajesh), Common (book, soldier), Abstract (courage, honesty), Collective (fleet, army, crew), Countable, Uncountable.
2. PRONOUN: Replaces a noun. Types: Personal (I/me, he/him, they/them), Possessive (my, his, their), Reflexive (myself, himself), Relative (who, which, that), Demonstrative (this, that, these, those), Interrogative (who, what, which).
3. VERB: Shows action or state. Types: Transitive (needs object), Intransitive (no object), Auxiliary/Modal (is, have, can, will, must).
4. ADJECTIVE: Modifies a noun. Types: Descriptive (brave soldier), Numeral (three ships), Possessive (his rank), Demonstrative (this medal).
5. ADVERB: Modifies a verb, adjective, or another adverb. Types: Manner (quickly), Time (now, yesterday), Place (here, there), Frequency (always, never), Degree (very, quite).
6. PREPOSITION: Shows relationship (in, on, at, by, with, for, from, to, through).
7. CONJUNCTION: Joins words/clauses. Coordinating (and, but, or, so), Subordinating (because, although, if, when), Correlative (both...and, either...or).
8. INTERJECTION: Expresses sudden emotion (Oh! Alas! Bravo! Hurrah!).

SUBJECT-VERB AGREEMENT (Key Rules):
— Singular subject → singular verb: The captain gives orders.
— Plural subject → plural verb: The sailors follow orders.
— Two subjects with 'and' → plural: Ram and Shyam are here.
— Two subjects with 'or/nor' → verb agrees with nearer subject: Neither the officer nor the cadets were present.
— Collective nouns usually singular: The team is ready. The fleet has arrived.
— Uncountable nouns → singular: News is important. Information is power.
— Subjects with 'each/every/either/neither/anyone/everyone' → singular: Each of the soldiers has a rifle.
— Subjects ending in -ics (mathematics, physics, economics) → singular.

MODAL AUXILIARIES:
Can = ability/permission (present): He can swim.
Could = ability/permission (past)/polite request: Could you help me?
May = possibility/formal permission: It may rain. May I come in?
Might = weaker possibility: He might come.
Should = advice/duty/expectation: You should study hard.
Must = strong obligation/deduction: You must carry ID. He must be tired.
Would = polite request/habitual past/conditional: Would you help me? He would walk 10 km daily.
Shall = future (British)/suggestion: Shall we begin?
Will = future/strong intention: I will serve the nation.
points: 8 Parts of Speech: Noun, Pronoun, Verb, Adjective, Adverb, Preposition, Conjunction, Interjection.
Noun types: Proper, Common, Abstract, Collective, Countable, Uncountable.
Singular subject → singular verb; Plural → plural verb.
'And' joining two subjects → plural verb; 'Or/Nor' → verb agrees with nearer subject.
Uncountable nouns (news, information, water) and -ics subjects → singular verb.
Each/every/either/neither/anyone/everyone → singular verb.
Transitive verb needs an object; intransitive does not.
Can = present ability; Could = past ability/polite request.
May = formal permission/possibility; Must = strong obligation.
Should = advice; Would = polite request or habitual past.
examples: Subject-verb: 'The news is shocking' (uncountable → singular). 'The fleet has arrived' (collective → singular).
Modal: 'You should revise daily' (advice). 'You must carry your ID' (obligation).
Agreement: 'Neither the captain nor the sailors were ready' (verb agrees with nearer subject: sailors).
Parts of speech: In 'She bravely led the mission', 'She'=pronoun, 'bravely'=adverb, 'led'=verb, 'mission'=noun.
Conjunction: 'He trained hard, yet he was not selected.' (yet = coordinating, showing contrast)
ag-1.summary: Grammar in context means applying rules to actual sentences. 8 parts of speech: noun, pronoun, verb, adjective, adverb, preposition, conjunction, interjection. Subject-verb agreement: singular with singular, plural with plural; 'and' → plural; 'or/nor' → nearer subject rules; uncountable/-ics/each/every → singular. Modals: can/could (ability), may/might (possibility), should (advice), must (obligation), would (request/habitual past).

questions.question: Which sentence shows correct subject-verb agreement?
options: Each of the soldiers has a rifle.
questions.explanation: 'Each' is always singular → 'has'. News, fleet, mathematics all take singular verbs too, but options A, B, D are wrong.

questions.question: Identify the modal that expresses strong obligation:
questions.explanation: 'Must' expresses strong necessity or obligation. 'Should' is weaker (advice). 'Can' = ability. 'May' = possibility.

questions.question: 'She bravely defended her post.' — 'bravely' is a:
questions.explanation: 'Bravely' modifies the verb 'defended' — it tells HOW she defended. Adverbs of manner answer 'how'.

questions.question: Neither the captain nor the sailors ___ ready.
questions.explanation: With 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject — 'sailors' is plural → 'were'.

questions.question: Which word is an abstract noun?
questions.explanation: Abstract nouns name intangible qualities or concepts. 'Courage' is abstract — you cannot see or touch it.

questions.question: Which sentence uses a modal for polite request?
questions.explanation: 'Could you please...?' is the standard polite request form. 'Must' is obligation; 'can' is ability; 'should' is advice.

questions.question: Identify the collective noun: 'The ___ of ships sailed past.'
questions.explanation: 'Fleet' is the specific collective noun for a group of ships/aircraft.

questions.question: Which part of speech is 'Bravo!' in 'Bravo! You passed!'?
questions.explanation: Interjections express sudden emotion. 'Bravo!' expresses approval/praise.

questions.question: The verb in 'She gave him a book' is:
questions.explanation: 'Gave' is transitive — it has an object ('him a book'). Transitive verbs need an object to complete their meaning.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence:
questions.explanation: After modal auxiliaries (can, could, may, must, should, will), always use the base form (infinitive without 'to').

questions.question: Which is an uncountable noun?
questions.explanation: 'Information' is uncountable — you cannot say 'an information' or 'two informations'. Takes singular verb.

questions.question: 'Although he tried hard, he failed.' — 'Although' is a:
questions.explanation: 'Although' is a subordinating conjunction — it introduces a subordinate/dependent clause showing contrast.

questions.question: Which modal expresses possibility in the future?
questions.explanation: 'Might' expresses weak/uncertain possibility. 'It might rain tomorrow' — it is possible but not certain.

questions.question: Identify the error: 'He gave advices to all of us.'
questions.explanation: 'Advice' is uncountable — no plural form. 'Advices' is incorrect. Correct: 'He gave advice to all of us.'

questions.question: The subject of 'Mathematics is my favourite subject' is:
questions.explanation: Although 'Mathematics' looks plural, it is a singular noun (ending in -ics) and takes a singular verb.

ip-1.title: Common Idioms and Their Meanings
ip-1.notes:
An idiom is a phrase whose overall meaning differs from the literal meaning of its individual words. Idioms are fixed expressions — you cannot change the words or their order.

COMPLETE LIST OF KEY IDIOMS FOR NEA:

A: A blessing in disguise = something bad that turns out good. A hard nut to crack = a difficult person or problem. A penny for your thoughts = asking what someone is thinking. At the drop of a hat = immediately, without hesitation. At loggerheads = in strong disagreement. At the eleventh hour = at the last possible moment.

B: Barking up the wrong tree = blaming the wrong person or pursuing wrong direction. Beat around the bush = avoid stating the main point. Bite off more than you can chew = take on more than you can handle. Bite the bullet = endure pain bravely. Bite the dust = fail or die. Break a leg = good luck. Break the ice = initiate conversation and ease tension. Burn bridges = permanently damage a relationship. Burn the midnight oil = work/study very late.

C: Call a spade a spade = speak plainly. Cast pearls before swine = offer something valuable to someone who doesn't appreciate it. Caught red-handed = discovered in the act of wrongdoing. Cost an arm and a leg = very expensive. Cross that bridge when you come to it = deal with the problem when it arises. Cut corners = do something carelessly to save time or money.

D: Die hard = difficult to change or give up. Don't judge a book by its cover = don't judge by appearances only. Down to earth = practical and realistic.

E: Every cloud has a silver lining = every bad situation has something positive. Every dog has its day = everyone has a moment of success.

F: Face the music = accept the consequences. Fall on deaf ears = be ignored. Feel under the weather = feel unwell. Fine-tooth comb = examine very carefully.

G: Get cold feet = become afraid at the last moment. Get out of hand = become uncontrollable. Get the ball rolling = start something. Give the benefit of the doubt = trust despite uncertainty.

H: Hard nut to crack = difficult problem or person. Hit the nail on the head = say exactly the right thing. Hit the sack = go to bed. Hold your horses = wait/slow down.

K: Kill two birds with one stone = solve two problems with one action. Know the ropes = be experienced in something.

L: Leave no stone unturned = try everything possible. Let sleeping dogs lie = avoid stirring up past trouble. Let the cat out of the bag = accidentally reveal a secret.

M: Make ends meet = manage finances with difficulty. Miss the boat = miss an opportunity.

N: Not beat around the bush = speak directly.

O: On the ball = alert and efficient. Once in a blue moon = very rarely. On thin ice = in a risky situation.

P: Pull someone's leg = joke with someone. Put your foot in it = say something embarrassing. Put your foot down = assert authority firmly.

R: Raining cats and dogs = raining very heavily.

S: Spill the beans = reveal a secret. Steal someone's thunder = take credit for another's achievement. Sit on the fence = remain undecided.

T: The last straw = the final problem that makes a situation unbearable. Through thick and thin = through all difficulties. Throw in the towel = admit defeat. Turn a blind eye = deliberately ignore something. Turn over a new leaf = change behaviour for the better.

U: Under the weather = feeling unwell.
points: Beat around the bush = avoid the main point; Hit the nail on the head = say exactly right.
Bite the bullet = endure bravely; Bite the dust = fail/die.
Break the ice = ease tension; Burn midnight oil = work very late.
Every cloud has a silver lining = positive in negative; Kill two birds = solve two at once.
Let the cat out of the bag = reveal secret; Spill the beans = reveal secret.
Once in a blue moon = very rarely; At the eleventh hour = at the last moment.
Get cold feet = become afraid; Throw in the towel = admit defeat.
Turn over a new leaf = change for better; Leave no stone unturned = try everything.
On thin ice = in risky situation; Cost an arm and a leg = very expensive.
Under the weather = unwell; Miss the boat = miss an opportunity.
examples: 'He burned the midnight oil for a week before the NEA exam.' = studied very late at night.
'She let the cat out of the bag about the surprise posting.' = accidentally revealed the secret.
'Every cloud has a silver lining — his injury led him to study even harder.' = positive came from negative.
'He beat around the bush for ten minutes before stating the real problem.' = avoided direct answer.
'The government left no stone unturned to rescue the sailors.' = tried every possible means.
ip-1.summary: Idioms are fixed expressions with non-literal meanings. Key NEA idioms: beat around the bush (avoid topic), hit the nail on the head (exactly right), burn midnight oil (study late), every cloud has a silver lining (positive in negative), let the cat out of the bag (reveal secret), once in a blue moon (rarely), get cold feet (become afraid), throw in the towel (admit defeat), turn over a new leaf (change for better), leave no stone unturned (try everything), on thin ice (risky situation).

questions.explanation: 'Beat around the bush' means to avoid saying what you really mean, talking around the subject.

questions.question: 'He got cold feet before the interview.' This means:

Every bad situation has some good in it

questions.question: What does 'once in a blue moon' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Once in a blue moon' means something that happens very rarely or almost never.

questions.question: 'He threw in the towel after three failed attempts.' This means:
options: He admitted defeat and gave up

options: Clear all stones from a path

questions.question: 'He hit the nail on the head with his analysis.' Meaning:
options: He said exactly the right thing

questions.question: What does 'break the ice' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Break the ice' means to do or say something to ease tension and start a conversation or activity.

questions.question: 'He is on thin ice with his commander.' This means:
options: He is in a risky or dangerous situation
questions.explanation: 'On thin ice' means to be in a risky or precarious situation where something might go wrong.

questions.question: What does 'miss the boat' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Miss the boat' means to miss an opportunity, often because of delay or lack of action.

questions.question: 'Let sleeping dogs lie' means:

questions.question: What does 'at the eleventh hour' mean?

voc-1.title: Word Meanings and Usage
voc-1.notes:
Vocabulary questions in NEA test your ability to understand word meanings in context, choose the correct word, and recognise synonyms and antonyms. A strong vocabulary is built through reading and systematic learning.

WORD MEANINGS IN CONTEXT — STRATEGY:
Even if you don't know a word, use context clues:
— Definition clue: 'The soldier showed valour, that is, exceptional bravery in battle.'
— Contrast clue: 'Unlike his timid brother, he was audacious.'
— Example clue: 'Aquatic animals like fish, dolphins, and whales...' (aquatic = water-living)
— Synonym clue: 'She was jubilant, or overjoyed, at the news.'

HIGH-FREQUENCY VOCABULARY FOR NEA:

ADJECTIVES:
Acrimonious = bitter/harsh in tone. Adept = highly skilled. Ambiguous = having two or more possible meanings. Benign = harmless/kind. Candid = frank and honest. Cogent = clear and convincing. Concise = brief and clear. Diligent = hardworking. Eminent = famous and respected. Enigmatic = mysterious. Erroneous = wrong/incorrect. Fastidious = very particular and demanding. Formidable = inspiring fear or respect due to impressive qualities. Frugal = careful with money. Gregarious = sociable. Imperious = bossy/domineering. Impetuous = acting without thinking. Incessant = never stopping. Indignant = angry at unfair treatment. Innate = inborn/natural. Judicious = showing good judgment. Meticulous = paying great attention to detail. Nonchalant = calm and relaxed, unconcerned. Obstinate = stubborn. Prudent = sensible and careful. Redundant = unnecessary/superfluous. Resilient = able to recover quickly. Salient = most noticeable or important. Shrewd = clever and practical. Tenacious = persistent, not giving up.

NOUNS:
Acumen = keen insight. Brevity = quality of being brief. Candour = frankness. Complacency = self-satisfaction and lack of effort. Dilemma = difficult choice between two options. Eloquence = fluent and persuasive speech. Empathy = understanding others' feelings. Equanimity = calmness under pressure. Facade = outward appearance concealing reality. Fervour = intense enthusiasm. Fortitude = courage in difficulty. Frugality = carefulness with money. Hubris = excessive pride leading to downfall. Ingenuity = cleverness in solving problems. Leniency = mildness in punishment. Magnanimity = generosity and forgiveness. Mediocrity = quality of being merely average. Parsimony = extreme stinginess. Perseverance = continued effort despite difficulty. Pragmatism = practical approach. Prowess = great skill or bravery. Rectitude = moral correctness. Sagacity = wisdom. Tenacity = persistence. Turbulence = instability/disturbance. Zeal = great energy and enthusiasm.

VERBS:
Abrogate = abolish officially. Ameliorate = make better. Castigate = criticise severely. Corroborate = confirm/support. Denigrate = unfairly criticise. Disseminate = spread widely. Elucidate = make clear. Exacerbate = make worse. Mitigate = make less severe. Rectify = put right. Repudiate = reject. Vindicate = clear of blame.
points: Use context clues: definition, contrast, example, or synonym clues.
Formidable = impressive and powerful; Tenacious = persistent; Prudent = sensible/careful.
Meticulous = very detailed/careful; Fastidious = very fussy; Diligent = hardworking.
Candid = frank; Eloquence = fluent speech; Equanimity = calmness under pressure.
Perseverance = continued effort; Fortitude = courage in difficulty; Zeal = enthusiasm.
Exacerbate = make worse; Mitigate = make less severe (opposites — common exam pair).
Corroborate = confirm; Elucidate = make clear; Disseminate = spread widely.
Hubris = excessive pride; Complacency = self-satisfaction without effort.
Sagacity = wisdom; Acumen = keen insight (business acumen = sharp business sense).
Ambiguous = having more than one meaning; Enigmatic = mysterious and hard to understand.
examples: Context: 'His cogent arguments convinced everyone.' = his clear and convincing arguments.
Context: 'She showed equanimity under fire.' = remained calm and composed under pressure.
Contrast clue: 'Unlike his reckless colleague, he was prudent in every decision.'
Usage: 'His tenacity earned him the selection despite three previous failures.'
Pair: 'The medicine mitigated the pain, though it did not cure the disease.' (mitigate = reduce)
voc-1.summary: Vocabulary questions test word meanings in context. Use context clues (definition, contrast, example, synonym). Key adjectives: formidable, tenacious, prudent, meticulous, candid, diligent, eminent. Key nouns: perseverance, fortitude, equanimity, acumen, eloquence, zeal. Key verbs: mitigate (reduce), exacerbate (worsen), corroborate (confirm), elucidate (clarify), disseminate (spread). Opposite pairs like mitigate/exacerbate and ambiguous/clear are commonly tested.

questions.question: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'TENACIOUS':
questions.explanation: 'Tenacious' means holding firmly to something — determined and persistent despite difficulties.

questions.question: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'MITIGATE':
questions.explanation: 'Mitigate' means to make something less severe or intense. Opposite of exacerbate.

questions.question: The word 'PRUDENT' means:
questions.explanation: 'Prudent' means acting with careful judgment and good sense — sensible and cautious.

questions.question: Choose the word opposite in meaning to 'EXACERBATE':
questions.explanation: 'Exacerbate' = make worse. Its antonym is 'mitigate' = make less severe.

questions.question: The word 'EQUANIMITY' means:
questions.explanation: 'Equanimity' = mental calmness and composure, especially in difficult situations.

questions.question: 'His COGENT arguments won the debate.' COGENT means:
questions.explanation: 'Cogent' means powerfully persuasive and clear — logically compelling.

questions.question: Choose the synonym of 'DILIGENT':
questions.explanation: 'Industrious' = hardworking and diligent — both describe someone who works with sustained effort.

questions.question: The word 'CORROBORATE' means:
questions.explanation: 'Corroborate' means to confirm or give support to a statement or theory.

questions.question: 'She showed great FORTITUDE during the crisis.' FORTITUDE means:
questions.explanation: 'Fortitude' means mental and emotional strength in facing adversity with courage.

questions.question: The word 'DISSEMINATE' means:
questions.explanation: 'Disseminate' means to spread or distribute information widely — to make it known broadly.

questions.question: 'An ENIGMATIC smile played on her lips.' ENIGMATIC means:
questions.explanation: 'Enigmatic' means mysterious, difficult to understand or interpret.

questions.question: The word 'ELOQUENCE' refers to:
questions.explanation: 'Eloquence' is the quality of being fluent, expressive, and persuasive in speech or writing.

ic-2.title: Election and Representation in India
ic-2.notes:
The Indian electoral system underpins democracy. Every eligible citizen participates in choosing representatives who form the government.

FUNDAMENTAL RIGHT TO VOTE:
Article 326 of the Constitution grants universal adult suffrage — every citizen aged 18+ has the right to vote, regardless of religion, race, caste, sex, or income. The voting age was reduced from 21 to 18 by the 61st Constitutional Amendment (1988).

ELECTION COMMISSION OF INDIA (ECI):
Established under Article 324. An independent constitutional body. Headed by the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC). The CEC has security of tenure — can only be removed by a process similar to removal of a Supreme Court judge (address by both Houses of Parliament). Ensures free, fair, and impartial elections.

TYPES OF ELECTIONS IN INDIA:
1. General Elections (Lok Sabha): Every 5 years. Direct election. First Past the Post (FPTP) system.
2. State Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha): Every 5 years per state.
3. Rajya Sabha elections: Indirect — by elected MLAs of states. Proportional Representation with Single Transferable Vote (STV).
4. Presidential election: Indirect — by elected MPs and MLAs. Proportional Representation.
5. Vice Presidential election: By elected MPs of both Houses.
6. By-elections: When a seat falls vacant mid-term.

LOK SABHA:
Max 552 seats (543 elected + up to 2 nominated Anglo-Indians — abolished by 104th Amendment, 2020).
Presiding officer: Speaker (elected by Lok Sabha members).
Minimum age: 25 years.
System: FPTP — candidate with most votes wins.
Term: 5 years (can be dissolved earlier by President on PM's advice).

RAJYA SABHA:
Max 250 (238 from states + 12 nominated by President).
Presiding officer: Vice President (ex-officio Chairman).
Permanent body — cannot be dissolved.
1/3 members retire every 2 years. Each member's term: 6 years.
Minimum age: 30 years.

MODEL CODE OF CONDUCT (MCC): Guidelines issued by ECI during elections to ensure fair campaigning. In force from announcement of election till results.

ELECTORAL ROLL: List of eligible voters maintained by ECI. Updated annually. Every citizen 18+ can register.
points: Article 326: Universal adult suffrage — every citizen 18+ can vote.
61st Amendment (1988) reduced voting age from 21 to 18.
ECI (Article 324): independent constitutional body ensuring free and fair elections.
CEC has security of tenure — removed like a Supreme Court judge.
General elections for Lok Sabha: every 5 years, FPTP system, direct election.
Lok Sabha: 543 elected seats, min age 25, Speaker as presiding officer.
Rajya Sabha: 250 seats, permanent body, 6-year terms, VP as Chairman, min age 30.
Presidential election: indirect, by elected MPs and MLAs, Proportional Representation.
Rajya Sabha elections: indirect by MLAs, Proportional Representation with STV.
Model Code of Conduct: ECI guidelines binding during election period.
examples: FPTP: In a 3-candidate Lok Sabha race with votes 45%, 35%, 20% — the candidate with 45% wins, even without majority.
By-election: When an MP dies, resigns, or is disqualified, a by-election is held for that constituency.
Rajya Sabha elections: UP sends more RS members than a smaller state due to proportional representation by state population.
Model Code: Once elections are announced, no new government schemes can be announced by ruling party.
Electoral Roll: As of 2024, India had over 96 crore registered voters — the world's largest electorate.
ic-2.summary: Article 326 gives all citizens 18+ the right to vote (since 1988's 61st Amendment). ECI (Article 324) is an independent body ensuring fair elections. Lok Sabha: 543 elected, 5-year term, FPTP, Speaker presides, min age 25. Rajya Sabha: 250 seats, permanent, 6-year terms, VP as Chairman, min age 30. Presidential election uses Proportional Representation by elected MPs and MLAs. Model Code of Conduct applies during election period.

ca-1.title: National Current Affairs
ca-1.notes:
National Current Affairs covers major events, government schemes, policies, and developments within India. The NEA exam tests your awareness of recent happenings in India across politics, economy, sports, and society.

KEY GOVERNMENT SCHEMES AND PROGRAMMES:
PM Gati Shakti: National Master Plan for multi-modal connectivity — integrating roads, railways, ports, airports.
PM Awas Yojana (PMAY): Housing for All. Urban and Rural variants. Target: affordable housing for economically weaker sections.
PM Kisan Samman Nidhi: Direct income support of ₹6,000/year in 3 instalments to eligible farmers.
Jal Jeevan Mission: Har Ghar Jal — piped drinking water to every rural household by 2024.
Swachh Bharat Mission: Cleanliness campaign, building toilets, achieving ODF (Open Defecation Free) status.
Ayushman Bharat (PM-JAY): Health insurance coverage of ₹5 lakh per family per year for poor families.
Digital India: Digitisation of government services and promoting digital literacy.
Make in India: Promoting manufacturing in India, attracting investments.
Stand Up India: Loans to SC/ST entrepreneurs and women.
Mudra Yojana: Micro-finance loans to small businesses under Shishu (up to ₹50k), Kishore (₹50k–₹5L), Tarun (₹5L–₹10L).
National Education Policy 2020 (NEP 2020): Major reform in education — 5+3+3+4 structure, mother-tongue instruction, coding from Class 6.
PM Vishwakarma: Support to artisans and craftspeople.
One Nation One Ration Card: Beneficiaries can access PDS ration from any FPS across India.

INDIA'S ECONOMY INDICATORS (approximate, for awareness):
GDP growth rate: India is one of the fastest-growing major economies (6–8% growth in recent years).
India's rank in Ease of Doing Business improved significantly.
UPI transactions: India is the global leader in real-time digital payments.
India overtook UK to become the 5th largest economy in the world.

INDIA IN GLOBAL FORUMS:
G20 Presidency: India held G20 Presidency in 2023. New Delhi Summit was held in September 2023. Theme: 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam' (One Earth, One Family, One Future).
SCO: India is a member of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation.
BRICS: India is a founding member.
Quad: India is part of the Quadrilateral Security Dialogue (India, USA, Japan, Australia).

ca-2.title: International Current Affairs
ca-2.notes:
International current affairs for NEA cover global events, international organisations, treaties, and India's role in the world. This section tests general awareness of major global developments.

INTERNATIONAL ORGANISATIONS:
United Nations (UN): Founded 1945. HQ: New York. 193 member nations. 6 official languages. Secretary-General: António Guterres (Portugal). 6 principal organs: General Assembly, Security Council, Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC), Secretariat, International Court of Justice, Trusteeship Council (inactive).
UN Security Council: 5 permanent members (P5) with veto power: USA, UK, France, Russia, China. 10 non-permanent members elected for 2-year terms.
UNESCO: Education, Science, Culture. HQ: Paris.
WHO: World Health Organisation. HQ: Geneva.
IMF: International Monetary Fund. HQ: Washington D.C.
World Bank: Development loans. HQ: Washington D.C.
WTO: World Trade Organisation. HQ: Geneva. Trade rules and dispute settlement.
NATO: North Atlantic Treaty Organisation. Military alliance. HQ: Brussels.
SCO: Shanghai Cooperation Organisation. India, China, Russia, Pakistan members.
ASEAN: 10 Southeast Asian nations. HQ: Jakarta.
G7: USA, UK, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, Canada (+ EU).
G20: 19 countries + EU. India hosted 2023 Presidency.

RECENT GLOBAL EVENTS (for awareness):
COP summits: Annual UN climate conferences. COP28 (2023) in Dubai, UAE.
Artificial Intelligence: AI governance becoming a global priority. UK AI Safety Summit (2023).
Ukraine-Russia conflict: Ongoing conflict affecting global energy and food security.
Israel-Gaza conflict: Significant humanitarian and geopolitical impact.
Expansion of BRICS: New members including Saudi Arabia, UAE, Ethiopia, Iran, Egypt, Argentina joined in 2024.
Taiwan Strait tensions: Rising US-China tensions over Taiwan's status.
Moon missions: India's Chandrayaan-3 successfully landed near the lunar south pole (August 2023) — India became the 4th country to land on Moon and 1st near south pole.

INDIA'S INTERNATIONAL RELATIONS:
India maintains 'strategic autonomy' — balancing relations with USA, Russia, and others.
India-USA: Comprehensive Global Strategic Partnership. Defence deals (MQ-9B drones, GE jet engine).
India-Russia: Traditional ally. Buys Russian oil at discounted rates.
India-China: Border disputes (Galwan 2020). LAC tensions ongoing.
points: UN founded 1945, HQ New York, 193 members. SG: António Guterres.
UNSC P5 (veto): USA, UK, France, Russia, China.
WHO (Geneva), IMF (Washington D.C.), WTO (Geneva), UNESCO (Paris).
G20: 19 countries + EU. India hosted 2023 Presidency.
SCO members include India, China, Russia, Pakistan.
Chandrayaan-3: India landed near Moon's south pole (Aug 2023) — 1st nation to do so.
BRICS expansion (2024): Saudi Arabia, UAE, Ethiopia, Iran, Egypt joined.
COP28 (2023): UN climate conference held in Dubai, UAE.
NATO: military alliance, HQ Brussels. India is not a member.
India's strategic autonomy: balances ties with USA, Russia, and others.
examples: Chandrayaan-3: Vikram lander and Pragyan rover made India the 4th country to land on Moon and 1st near the south pole.
BRICS 2024: expanded from 5 to 11 members with new additions from Middle East and Africa.
COP28 Dubai: agreement on transitioning away from fossil fuels — a landmark in climate diplomacy.
India-USA: Signed MQ-9B Predator drone deal worth ~$3 billion for Indian Navy and Air Force.
UN Security Council reform: India has been pushing for permanent membership for decades.
ca-2.summary: International current affairs cover UN (founded 1945, HQ New York, SG Guterres), UNSC P5 veto powers (USA, UK, France, Russia, China), and major organisations: WHO (Geneva), IMF/World Bank (Washington), WTO/UN/UNESCO (Geneva/New York/Paris). Key recent events: Chandrayaan-3 (India 1st to land near Moon's south pole, Aug 2023), BRICS expansion (2024), COP28 (Dubai 2023). India maintains strategic autonomy while partnering with USA, Russia, and others.

ca-3.title: Sports, Awards and Personalities
ca-3.notes:
This topic covers major sports events, India's achievements, national awards, and prominent personalities relevant to the NEA exam.

MAJOR SPORTS EVENTS AND INDIA'S PERFORMANCE:

Cricket:
ICC World Cup 2023: Held in India. Australia won the final, defeating India.
ICC T20 World Cup 2024: Held in USA and West Indies. India won, defeating South Africa in the final.

Olympics:
Paris Olympics 2024: India sent 117 athletes. India won 6 medals — 1 Silver, 5 Bronze. Neeraj Chopra won Silver in Javelin Throw.
Previous Tokyo Olympics 2020 (held 2021): India won 7 medals — Neeraj Chopra won India's first ever Olympic Gold in Athletics (Javelin).

Asian Games 2023 (Hangzhou, China): India won 107 medals (28 Gold, 38 Silver, 41 Bronze) — best-ever performance.

Chess: D. Gukesh became the youngest World Chess Champion in history (2024), defeating Ding Liren.

Badminton: PV Sindhu — two-time Olympic medalist. Saina Nehwal — India's badminton icon.

Wrestling: Bajrang Punia, Vinesh Phogat — prominent grapplers.

NATIONAL AWARDS:
Bharat Ratna: Highest civilian award. 2024 recipients: LK Advani, Chaudhary Charan Singh, PV Narasimha Rao, MS Swaminathan (posthumous), Karpoori Thakur (posthumous).
Padma Awards: Padma Vibhushan (2nd highest), Padma Bhushan (3rd), Padma Shri (4th). Announced on Republic Day eve.

Military Awards:
Paramvir Chakra: Highest gallantry award. Given for most distinguished acts of valour in the face of the enemy.
Vir Chakra: 3rd highest. Mahavir Chakra: 2nd highest.
Ashok Chakra: Highest peacetime gallantry.

INTERNATIONAL AWARDS:

Man Booker Prize: Prestigious English literature award.
Oscar (Academy Award): Film industry.
Grammy: Music.

President Droupadi Murmu: 15th President of India. First tribal woman president.

st-1.title: Recent Inventions and Discoveries
st-1.notes:

WWW (World Wide Web): Tim Berners-Lee (1989)

Radio: Guglielmo Marconi (1895); JC Bose also demonstrated wireless transmission (1895)

Electricity (AC): Nikola Tesla; Practical use of electric light: Thomas Edison

Relativiy (E=mc²): Albert Einstein (1905)
Periodic table: Dmitri Mendeleev (1869)
Bharat Ratna winners in science: C.V. Raman, APJ Abdul Kalam, Homi Bhabha

RECENT DISCOVERIES (2022-2024):
JWST (James Webb Space Telescope): Launched Dec 2021 by NASA/ESA/CSA. Observing early universe, exoplanets, deep field images — much more powerful than Hubble.
AI Breakthroughs: ChatGPT (OpenAI, 2022) demonstrated conversational AI. GPT-4 (2023). Google Gemini (2023). These use Large Language Models (LLMs).
CRISPR gene editing: Revolutionising medicine — first CRISPR-based therapy for sickle cell disease approved by FDA (2023).
Malaria Vaccine (R21/Matrix-M): WHO recommended (2023) — first high-efficacy malaria vaccine.
Fusion Energy: National Ignition Facility (USA) achieved net energy gain from nuclear fusion (2022) — landmark in clean energy.
Artificial General Intelligence (AGI): Research milestone — AI systems increasingly approaching human-level reasoning.
India's achievements: Chandrayaan-3 (lunar south pole, 2023), Aditya-L1 (solar observatory, 2023), XPoSat (X-ray polarimetry satellite, 2024).

INDIAN SCIENTISTS:

APJ Abdul Kalam: Father of India's missile programme (AGNI, PRITHVI).
Homi Bhabha: Father of India's nuclear programme.
Vikram Sarabhai: Father of India's space programme.
Srinivasa Ramanujan: Mathematical genius — number theory, infinite series.

st-2.title: Space Technology and ISRO Missions
st-2.notes:
India's space programme through ISRO has achieved global recognition. This topic covers ISRO's missions, space technology, and India's space milestones.

ISRO — INDIAN SPACE RESEARCH ORGANISATION:
Founded: 1969 by Dr. Vikram Sarabhai
Headquarters: Bengaluru
First satellite: Aryabhata (1975)
First Indian in space: Rakesh Sharma (1984, Soviet Soyuz T-11)
Launch sites: Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC), Sriharikota, Andhra Pradesh (primary); Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launching Station (TERLS), Kerala

MAJOR ISRO LAUNCH VEHICLES:
SLV (Satellite Launch Vehicle): First Indian rocket. SLV-3 (1980) — first successful launch.
ASLV (Augmented SLV): 4-stage solid rocket.
PSLV (Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle): India's most reliable rocket. Launched in 1993. 4 stages (alternating solid/liquid). Used for LEO, SSO missions. Launched Chandrayaan-1, Mars Orbiter Mission.
GSLV Mk II: 3-stage rocket with indigenous cryogenic engine. For GEO orbit.
LVM3 (Launch Vehicle Mark 3 / GSLV Mk III): Heaviest Indian rocket. 3 stages. Used for Chandrayaan-2, Chandrayaan-3, OneWeb commercial launches.

MAJOR MISSIONS:
Aryabhata (1975): First Indian satellite. Named after ancient mathematician.
SLV-3 (1980): First successful Indian satellite launch vehicle.
IRS (Indian Remote Sensing): Series of Earth observation satellites.
INSAT: Indian National Satellite System — communication and meteorology.
Oceansat, Cartosat, Resourcesat: Earth observation series.
Chandrayaan-1 (2008): India's first Moon mission. Discovered water molecules on Moon.
Mangalyaan / MOM (2013): Mars Orbiter Mission — India became 4th to reach Mars, 1st Asian country, and succeeded on first attempt. Cost less than Hollywood film Gravity (~₹450 crore).
Chandrayaan-2 (2019): Orbiter succeeded. Vikram lander crash-landed.
Chandrayaan-3 (2023): Successfully landed near lunar south pole. Pragyan rover deployed. India became 4th country on Moon and 1st near south pole.
Aditya-L1 (2023): India's first solar mission. Placed at L1 Lagrange point to study the Sun continuously.
Gaganyaan: India's first human spaceflight mission. Planned for 2025. 3 astronauts for 3 days in LEO.
XPoSat (2024): X-ray Polarimeter Satellite — studies polarisation of X-rays from cosmic sources.

SPACE CONCEPTS:
Geostationary Orbit (GEO): 35,786 km above equator. Satellite appears stationary. Used for TV/communication.
Polar Orbit: Passes over poles. Covers entire Earth. Used for remote sensing, weather.
Sun-Synchronous Orbit (SSO): Special polar orbit — satellite crosses equator at same local time daily. Consistent lighting for imaging.
Lagrange Points: Points in space where gravitational forces balance centripetal force. L1 (between Sun and Earth) — ideal for solar observation.
points: ISRO founded 1969 (Vikram Sarabhai). HQ: Bengaluru. Launch site: Sriharikota.
First Indian satellite: Aryabhata (1975). First Indian in space: Rakesh Sharma (1984).
PSLV: workhorse rocket, 4-stage, polar orbits. LVM3: heaviest Indian rocket.
Chandrayaan-1 (2008): discovered water on Moon. MOM (2013): India 1st Asian country to reach Mars.
Chandrayaan-3 (2023): successful lunar south pole landing — India 4th on Moon, 1st near south pole.
Aditya-L1 (2023): India's solar mission, placed at L1 Lagrange point.
Gaganyaan: India's first crewed mission, planned 2025, 3 astronauts, 3 days in LEO.
GEO: 35,786 km, satellite appears stationary. Used for communication and weather.
SSO: crosses equator at same local time — ideal for Earth observation.
L1 Lagrange Point: between Sun and Earth — ideal for continuous solar observation.
examples: MOM cost ₹450 crore — cheaper than many Hollywood movies, demonstrating ISRO's frugal innovation.
Chandrayaan-3's Pragyan rover drove on the lunar surface for ~100 metres, analysing soil composition.
PSLV-C37 (2017) launched 104 satellites in a single mission — world record at the time.
Aditya-L1 carries 7 payloads to study solar corona, solar winds, and space weather.
Gaganyaan astronauts (Vyomanauts) are being trained in Russia and India for the crewed mission.
st-2.summary: ISRO (1969, Bengaluru) has achieved: Aryabhata first satellite (1975), SLV-3 first rocket (1980), Chandrayaan-1 discovered water on Moon (2008), MOM — first Asian Mars mission (2013), Chandrayaan-3 — lunar south pole landing (2023), Aditya-L1 solar mission (2023). PSLV is the workhorse; LVM3 is the heavy-lift rocket. GEO (35,786 km) for communication; SSO for Earth imaging; L1 for solar observation. Gaganyaan — crewed mission planned for 2025.

questions.question: PSLV-C37 (2017) set a world record by launching:

questions.question: LVM3 (GSLV Mk III) is notable for:

questions.question: Sun-Synchronous Orbit (SSO) is useful for:

st-3.title: Defence Technology Developments
st-3.notes:
India has been rapidly advancing its defence technology. This is a crucial topic for NEA as it directly relates to the Indian Navy and defence services.

INDIAN MISSILE SYSTEMS:
Agni series: Long-range ballistic missiles. Agni-V has range 5,000+ km (ICBM class). Agni-VI under development.
Prithvi series: Short-range surface-to-surface missiles. Prithvi-I (army), Prithvi-II (air force), Dhanush (naval variant).
BrahMos: Supersonic cruise missile (Mach 2.8–3.0). Joint venture with Russia. Range: 290–500+ km. Fired from land, sea, submarine, and air. World's fastest operational cruise missile.
Astра: India's indigenous BVR (Beyond Visual Range) air-to-air missile. Mk-1 (110 km range), Mk-2 (160 km) under development.
NAG: Anti-tank missile. HELINA is helicopter-launched version.
NirBhay: Sub-sonic long-range cruise missile (1,000 km range).
Shaurya: Hypersonic surface-to-surface missile.
K-15/B-05/Sagarika: Submarine-launched ballistic missile (SLBM). Range 700–750 km.
K-4: SLBM with 3,500 km range — for INS Arihant class submarines.

NAVAL DEVELOPMENTS:
INS Vikrant (IAC-1): India's first domestically built aircraft carrier. Commissioned September 2022. Kochi.
INS Vikramaditya: Acquired from Russia (former INS Gorshkov). Operational aircraft carrier.
INS Arihant: India's first nuclear-powered ballistic missile submarine (SSBN). Operational.
INS Arighat: Second SSBN. Commissioned 2024.
INS Vela, INS Vagir, INS Vagsheer: Kalvari-class submarines (Scorpene design, French technology).
P-75I: Programme for 6 more advanced submarines.
Project-75: 6 Kalvari-class submarines — 5 delivered, 1 remaining.
P-17A: Stealth frigates (7 ships). Advanced technology.
MH-60R Seahawk: Multi-role naval helicopters — 24 procured from USA.
P-8I Poseidon: Long-range maritime patrol aircraft. Used for ASW and surveillance.
MQ-9B SeaGuardian: Drone for maritime surveillance.

AIR FORCE:
Rafale: 36 fighter jets acquired from France. Inducted 2020-2022.
Tejas Mk-1A: Indigenous Light Combat Aircraft. Orders for 83 aircraft.
Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft (AMCA): 5th generation stealth fighter under development.
S-400 Triumf: Advanced air defence missile system acquired from Russia.

ARMY:
Arjun Mk-1A: Advanced main battle tank. Indigenously developed.
K9 Vajra: Self-propelled howitzer.
Pinaka: Multi-barrel rocket launcher system.
DHRUV: Advanced Light Helicopter (ALH) — indigenously built by HAL.

DRDO: Defence Research and Development Organisation. Develops indigenous defence systems.
HAL: Hindustan Aeronautics Limited. Develops aircraft (Tejas, Dhruv, LCA).

in-1.title: Indian Navy — Structure and Ranks
in-1.notes:
Understanding the structure and ranks of the Indian Navy is fundamental knowledge for any NEA aspirant.

INDIAN NAVY — OVERVIEW:
Founded: 26 January 1950 (Republic Day, formal establishment).
Motto: 'Sham No Varunah' (meaning 'May the Lord of the Seas be auspicious unto us' — from Vedic scripture).
Headquarters: Integrated Defence Staff Headquarters, New Delhi.
Currently one of the most capable naval forces in the world — ranked among top 7 globally.

NAVAL COMMANDS:
1. Western Naval Command (WNC): HQ Mumbai. Commander-in-Chief: Flag Officer Commanding-in-Chief, Western Naval Command (FOCINCWEST).
2. Eastern Naval Command (ENC): HQ Visakhapatnam (Vizag).
3. Southern Naval Command (SNC): HQ Kochi. This is also the Training Command — INS Zamorin, INS Garuda, INS Dronacharya.
4. Andaman and Nicobar Command (ANC): HQ Port Blair. India's only Tri-Service command.

NAVAL RANKS (from highest to lowest):

FLAG OFFICERS (Officers):
Admiral of the Fleet (5 stars) — ceremonial, rarely conferred.
Admiral (4 stars) — Chief of Naval Staff (CNS) rank.
Vice Admiral (3 stars)
Rear Admiral (2 stars)
Commodore (1 broad stripe)

CAPTAIN/COMMANDER:
Captain
Commander
Lieutenant Commander

SUBALTERN OFFICERS:
Lieutenant
Sub Lieutenant
Midshipman (trainee officer)

SAILOR RANKS:
Master Chief Petty Officer (MCPO)
Chief Petty Officer (CPO)
Petty Officer (PO)
Leading Seaman
Seaman I
Seaman II (Entry level)

BRANCHES OF INDIAN NAVY:
1. Executive Branch: Ship command, navigation, weapons.
2. Engineering Branch: Propulsion, machinery.
3. Electrical Branch: Electrical and electronics systems.
4. Naval Architecture Branch: Ship design and construction.
5. Education Branch: Teaching and training.
6. Logistics Branch: Supply, administration.
7. Medical Branch: Health services.
8. MARCOS (Marine Commandos): Special Operations Force.

NAVAL ACADEMY:
INS Zamorin: Indian Naval Academy, Ezhimala, Kerala — premier training establishment for Naval Officers.
points: Indian Navy founded 26 January 1950. Motto: 'Sham No Varunah'.
4 Commands: Western (Mumbai), Eastern (Vizag), Southern (Kochi), ANC (Port Blair).
ANC (Port Blair) is India's only tri-service command.
Chief of Naval Staff holds rank of Admiral (4 stars).
Rank hierarchy (top): Admiral → Vice Admiral → Rear Admiral → Commodore → Captain.
Officer ranks: Admiral, Vice Admiral, Rear Admiral, Commodore, Captain, Commander, Lt Cdr, Lt, Sub-Lt, Midshipman.
Sailor ranks: MCPO → CPO → PO → Leading Seaman → Seaman I → Seaman II.
Branches: Executive, Engineering, Electrical, Naval Architecture, Education, Logistics, Medical, MARCOS.
MARCOS: Marine Commandos — Navy's special operations force.
INS Zamorin at Ezhimala, Kerala is the Indian Naval Academy — trains officer cadets.
examples: The CNS holds the rank of Admiral — 4-star officer, the highest active naval rank.
A newly commissioned officer holds the rank of Sub Lieutenant.
The Eastern Naval Command is responsible for Bay of Bengal, monitoring Chinese navy activity.
MARCOS have participated in Operation Cactus (Maldives 1988) and anti-piracy operations.
INS Zamorin (Naval Academy, Ezhimala) trains INA and BTECH (Cadet) entry officers.
in-1.summary: Indian Navy (est. 26 Jan 1950, motto: Sham No Varunah) has 4 commands: Western (Mumbai), Eastern (Vizag), Southern (Kochi, training), ANC (Port Blair, tri-service). Rank ladder: Admiral (CNS) → Vice Admiral → Rear Admiral → Commodore → Captain → Commander → Lt Cdr → Lt → Sub Lt → Midshipman. Sailor ranks: MCPO → CPO → PO → LS → Seaman. Branches include Executive, Engineering, Electrical, MARCOS (special ops). INS Zamorin (Ezhimala) is the Naval Academy.

in-3.title: Naval Operations and Achievements
in-3.notes:
The Indian Navy has a proud history of operations and achievements that reflect its growing strength and capability.

HISTORIC OPERATIONS:

1971 WAR OPERATIONS:
Operation Trident (4-5 December 1971): Attack on Karachi harbour. INS Nipat, INS Nirghat, INS Veer used Styx missiles (P-15). First time in naval history that anti-ship missiles were used in a naval attack. Sank PNS Khyber, PNS Muhafiz and destroyed fuel storage. Success led to celebration — 4 December as Indian Navy Day.

Operation Python (8-9 December 1971): Second strike on Karachi. INS Trishul, Vinash used Styx missiles. Destroyed POL (Petroleum, Oil, Lubricants) tankers and shore installations. PNS Dacca damaged.

INS Vikrant (the original): During 1971 war, INS Vikrant (first) blockaded East Pakistan's sea lanes, preventing resupply and cutting off Pakistan from the East — crucial contribution to Bangladesh's liberation.

OPERATION CACTUS (1988): India saved the Maldives government from a coup attempt. INS Godavari and aircraft carrier INS Viraat deployed. MARCOS commandos played key role. Restored President Gayoom to power within hours.

OPERATION VIJAY (1999 Kargil): Indian Navy maintained blockade of Pakistani ports, preventing resupply. Demonstrated power projection.

ANTI-PIRACY OPERATIONS:
Started 2008 in Gulf of Aden. Indian Navy ships have foiled 100+ piracy attempts. Rescued many merchant vessels including MV Alakrana, MV Suez.
Operation Sankalp (2019): Protecting Indian merchant shipping in Persian Gulf during US-Iran tensions.
Operation Kaveri (2023): Evacuation of Indian nationals from Sudan during civil war.

HUMANITARIAN OPERATIONS:
Operation Rainbow (2004 Tsunami): India led relief operations in Andaman, Maldives, Sri Lanka, Indonesia.
Operation Poomalai (1987): Humanitarian airlift to Tamil civilians in Sri Lanka.

ACHIEVEMENTS:
Indian Navy became the 7th navy in the world to operate two aircraft carriers simultaneously.
INS Tir and Tarangini: Sail training ships — trainees circumnavigate the globe.
World's first all-woman circumnavigation: INSV Tarini — 6 women officers completed in 2018.
points: Indian Navy Day: 4 December — commemorating Operation Trident (1971 Karachi attack).
Operation Trident: first use of anti-ship missiles in naval combat. Sank PNS Khyber.
INS Vikrant (1971): blockaded East Pakistan, pivotal in Bangladesh liberation.
Operation Cactus (1988): saved Maldives from coup — MARCOS and INS Viraat deployed.
Anti-piracy ops since 2008: Indian Navy protects merchant shipping in Gulf of Aden.
Operation Sankalp (2019): protected Indian shipping in Persian Gulf.
Operation Kaveri (2023): evacuated Indians from Sudan during civil war.
2004 Tsunami: India led regional relief under Operation Rainbow.
INSV Tarini (2018): 6 women officers completed first all-woman circumnavigation of globe.
India among few navies operating 2 aircraft carriers simultaneously.
examples: 4 December 1971: INS Nipat's Styx missiles hit Karachi — the fuel fires burned for days, clearly visible to city residents.
Operation Cactus: India's rapid response (within 12 hours) to Maldives coup attempt — showed India's strategic reach.
Anti-piracy: INS Tabar sank a pirate vessel in 2008 — first direct combat sinking.
INSV Tarini voyage: departed Goa Oct 2017, returned May 2018 — over 22,000 nautical miles.
Operation Kaveri (2023): evacuated 3,000+ Indians from Port Sudan during Sudan civil war.
in-3.summary: Indian Navy Day = 4 December (Operation Trident, 1971). Operation Trident: first anti-ship missile attack in naval history, hit Karachi. INS Vikrant (1971) blockaded East Pakistan. Operation Cactus (1988): saved Maldives from coup with MARCOS. Anti-piracy ops since 2008 in Gulf of Aden. Operation Sankalp (2019) in Persian Gulf. Operation Kaveri (2023) evacuated Indians from Sudan. INSV Tarini (2018): first all-woman global circumnavigation. India operates 2 aircraft carriers — a milestone for any navy.

in-4.title: Navy Motto, Flag and History
in-4.notes:
The symbols, flag, motto, and historical milestones of the Indian Navy reflect its heritage, pride, and tradition.

INDIAN NAVY MOTTO:
'Sham No Varunah' (Sanskrit: शं नो वरुणः)
Meaning: 'May the Lord of the Waters be auspicious unto us.'
Source: Rig Veda (Book VII, Hymn 35) — 'Sham no Mitra sham Varunah' (May Mitra and Varuna be auspicious to us).
Varuna: Vedic deity of water, sky, and cosmic order. Symbol of the Navy's ancient connection to the seas.

INDIAN NAVAL ENSIGN (FLAG):
The Indian Navy flies a distinctive White Ensign.
Pre-2022: White flag with George Cross (red cross from British colonial era) and Indian tricolour in canton. This had traces of colonial legacy.
2022 (Navy Day, 2 September 2022): New Naval Ensign unveiled by PM Narendra Modi during INS Vikrant commissioning. The colonial cross was removed.
New Ensign: White background with the Indian National Flag (tricolour) in the upper canton (top-left), and the Naval Crest at the lower fly (right). The Naval Crest features an octagonal shape inspired by Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj's royal seal (Rajmudra).
Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj: Revered as the 'Father of the Indian Navy' — he built a naval fleet on the western coast to protect Maratha territories in the 17th century.

HISTORY OF INDIAN NAVY:
3rd Century BC: Kautilya's Arthashastra mentions a 'Navadhyaksha' (Superintendent of Ships).
1612: British East India Company's first naval battle against Portuguese in Surat — foundation of colonial navy.
1671: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj built warships and fortified coastal bases (Sindhudurg, Vijaydurg).
1748: Maratha Navy under Kanhoji Angre was a dominant naval force on western coast.
1830: British reorganised Indian navy as 'Indian Navy' then 'Her Majesty's Indian Marine'.
1934: Royal Indian Navy established.
26 Jan 1950: Independent Republic of India — Indian Navy formally established.
1961: Liberation of Goa — Indian Navy supported land forces.
4 Dec 1971: Operation Trident — Indian Navy Day.
1988: Operation Cactus — Maldives.
2016: INS Arihant operational — nuclear triad complete.
2022: INS Vikrant commissioned — India joins elite carrier nations.

CHHATRAPATI SHIVAJI MAHARAJ AND NAVY:
Built India's first organised naval fleet in 17th century.
Constructed over 200 warships.
Fortified coastal forts: Sindhudurg, Vijaydurg, Jaigad.
INS Shivaji (Lonavala) — technical training establishment named after him.
IMD (Indian Maritime Doctrine) acknowledges his legacy.
points: Motto: 'Sham No Varunah' = 'May the Lord of Waters be auspicious unto us' (Rig Veda).
Varuna = Vedic deity of water. Mitra and Varuna are invoked in the motto's source hymn.
New Naval Ensign unveiled 2 September 2022 (INS Vikrant commissioning) — removed colonial cross.
New ensign: tricolour in canton + octagonal crest inspired by Shivaji's royal seal.
Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj = 'Father of the Indian Navy' — built organised naval fleet in 17th century.
Shivaji built Sindhudurg, Vijaydurg coastal forts and over 200 warships.
Indian Navy formally established 26 January 1950.
4 December = Indian Navy Day (Operation Trident 1971).
1934: Royal Indian Navy established under British India.
INS Shivaji (Lonavala): technical training establishment named after Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj.
examples: The old ensign had a George Cross (red cross) — a reminder of British colonial heritage of Royal Indian Navy.
On 2 September 2022, PM Modi unveiled the new ensign while commissioning INS Vikrant.
Shivaji's Sindhudurg fort (built 1664-67) in the Arabian Sea is a maritime heritage site.
Varuna features in the Navy's motto, badge, and is the name of the Indian Navy's weather prediction centre.
Kanhoji Angre controlled sea lanes along Maharashtra coast — even British paid tribute to his naval power.
in-4.summary: Indian Navy motto: 'Sham No Varunah' (Rig Veda) — May Varuna (Lord of Waters) be auspicious to us. New Naval Ensign (2022): tricolour in canton + octagonal crest inspired by Shivaji's seal — replaced colonial George Cross. Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj = Father of the Indian Navy (17th century fleet, coastal forts). Indian Navy established 26 Jan 1950. Navy Day: 4 December. Key milestones: 1971 (Operation Trident), 1988 (Operation Cactus), 2022 (INS Vikrant commissioned).

trig-2.title: Trigonometric Ratios of Standard Angles
trig-2.notes:
The six trigonometric ratios — sin, cos, tan, cosec, sec, cot — have exact values at standard angles 0°, 30°, 45°, 60°, and 90°. These must be memorised for solving exam problems quickly.

STANDARD VALUES TABLE:
         0°      30°       45°       60°       90°
sin:     0       1/2      √2/2      √3/2       1
cos:     1      √3/2      √2/2      1/2        0
tan:     0      1/√3       1        √3       undef
cosec:  undef    2        √2      2/√3        1
sec:     1      2/√3      √2        2        undef
cot:   undef    √3         1       1/√3       0

MEMORY TRICK for sin:
0° = √0/2 = 0
30° = √1/2 = 1/2
45° = √2/2 = 1/√2
60° = √3/2
90° = √4/2 = 1
For cos, the sequence reverses: cos 0°=1, cos 30°=√3/2, cos 45°=√2/2, cos 60°=1/2, cos 90°=0

KEY IDENTITIES (Pythagorean):
sin²θ + cos²θ = 1
1 + tan²θ = sec²θ
1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ

COMPLEMENTARY ANGLES:
sin θ = cos(90°−θ)      cos θ = sin(90°−θ)
tan θ = cot(90°−θ)      cot θ = tan(90°−θ)
sec θ = cosec(90°−θ)    cosec θ = sec(90°−θ)

QUADRANT SIGN RULE (All Silver Tea Cups):
Q1 (0–90°): All positive
Q2 (90–180°): Sin positive
Q3 (180–270°): Tan positive
Q4 (270–360°): Cos positive
points: cos values are sin values in reverse order.
tan 30°=1/√3, tan 45°=1, tan 60°=√3; tan 0°=0, tan 90°=undefined.
Pythagorean identity: sin²θ+cos²θ=1; 1+tan²θ=sec²θ; 1+cot²θ=cosec²θ.
Complementary: sin θ = cos(90°−θ), tan θ = cot(90°−θ).
ASTC rule: Q1=All, Q2=Sin, Q3=Tan, Q4=Cos positive.
cosec = 1/sin; sec = 1/cos; cot = 1/tan.
Memory for sin: numerators under √ go 0,1,2,3,4 divided by 2.
examples: If sinθ = 3/5, find cosθ: cos²θ = 1−9/25 = 16/25, cosθ = 4/5
trig-2.summary: Standard trigonometric values: sin 30°=1/2, 45°=1/√2, 60°=√3/2, 90°=1; cos is sin reversed. tan 30°=1/√3, 45°=1, 60°=√3. Three Pythagorean identities. Complementary angle: sin θ=cos(90°−θ). Quadrant signs: All Silver Tea Cups. Memorise the table — every NEA maths question uses these values.

trig-3.title: Trigonometric Identities and Applications
trig-3.notes:
Trigonometric identities are equations that hold true for all values of the angle. They are used to simplify expressions, prove other identities, and solve equations.

FUNDAMENTAL IDENTITIES:
1. sin²θ + cos²θ = 1  →  sin²θ = 1−cos²θ  →  cos²θ = 1−sin²θ
2. 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ  →  sec²θ − tan²θ = 1
3. 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ  →  cosec²θ − cot²θ = 1

QUOTIENT IDENTITIES:
tanθ = sinθ/cosθ       cotθ = cosθ/sinθ

RECIPROCAL IDENTITIES:
sinθ × cosecθ = 1      cosθ × secθ = 1      tanθ × cotθ = 1

ALLIED ANGLE IDENTITIES:
sin(−θ) = −sinθ         cos(−θ) = cosθ          tan(−θ) = −tanθ
sin(90°−θ) = cosθ       cos(90°−θ) = sinθ       tan(90°−θ) = cotθ
sin(90°+θ) = cosθ       cos(90°+θ) = −sinθ      tan(90°+θ) = −cotθ
sin(180°−θ) = sinθ      cos(180°−θ) = −cosθ     tan(180°−θ) = −tanθ
sin(180°+θ) = −sinθ     cos(180°+θ) = −cosθ     tan(180°+θ) = tanθ
sin(360°−θ) = −sinθ     cos(360°−θ) = cosθ

SUM AND DIFFERENCE FORMULAS:
sin(A+B) = sinA cosB + cosA sinB
sin(A−B) = sinA cosB − cosA sinB
cos(A+B) = cosA cosB − sinA sinB
cos(A−B) = cosA cosB + sinA sinB
tan(A+B) = (tanA+tanB)/(1−tanA tanB)
tan(A−B) = (tanA−tanB)/(1+tanA tanB)

DOUBLE ANGLE FORMULAS:
sin 2A = 2 sinA cosA
cos 2A = cos²A − sin²A = 1 − 2sin²A = 2cos²A − 1
tan 2A = 2tanA/(1−tan²A)

APPLICATION — HEIGHT AND DISTANCE:
Angle of Elevation: angle looking upward from horizontal.
Angle of Depression: angle looking downward from horizontal.
tanθ = Opposite/Adjacent = height/horizontal distance
points: sin²θ+cos²θ=1 is the most fundamental identity — derive others from it.
sec²θ−tan²θ=1 and cosec²θ−cot²θ=1 are the other Pythagorean forms.
sinθ×cosecθ=1; cosθ×secθ=1; tanθ×cotθ=1 (reciprocal identities).
sin(A+B)=sinAcosB+cosAsinB; cos(A+B)=cosAcosB−sinAsinB.
sin2A=2sinAcosA; cos2A=cos²A−sin²A=1−2sin²A=2cos²A−1.
sin(90°−θ)=cosθ; cos(90°−θ)=sinθ (complement).
sin(180°−θ)=sinθ; cos(180°−θ)=−cosθ.
Angle of elevation: observer looks UP. Angle of depression: observer looks DOWN.
For height & distance: tan(angle)=height/base distance.
At 45°: height = base distance (since tan45°=1).
examples: Prove: (1+sinθ)(1−sinθ) = cos²θ → LHS = 1−sin²θ = cos²θ = RHS ✓
Height & distance: A tower casts shadow 100m at elevation 30°. Height=100×tan30°=100/√3≈57.7m
Simplify: sin²25°+sin²65°=sin²25°+cos²25°=1 (since sin65°=cos25°)
trig-3.summary: Three Pythagorean identities: sin²θ+cos²θ=1, sec²−tan²=1, cosec²−cot²=1. Sum formulas: sin(A+B)=sinAcosB+cosAsinB, cos(A+B)=cosAcosB−sinAsinB. Double angle: sin2A=2sinAcosA, cos2A=cos²A−sin²A. Allied angles: sin(90°−θ)=cosθ, sin(180°−θ)=sinθ. Applications: angle of elevation/depression with tan = height/distance.

alg-1.title: HCF and LCM
alg-1.notes:
HCF (Highest Common Factor) and LCM (Lowest Common Multiple) are fundamental concepts in number theory.

HCF (also called GCD — Greatest Common Divisor):
The largest number that divides two or more numbers exactly.

METHODS TO FIND HCF:
1. Prime Factorisation: Express each number as a product of prime factors. HCF = product of COMMON prime factors with LOWEST powers.
   Example: 12=2²×3, 18=2×3². HCF = 2¹×3¹ = 6

2. Division Method (Euclidean Algorithm):
   Divide larger by smaller, then divide divisor by remainder, repeat until remainder=0.
   Last divisor = HCF.
   Example: HCF(48,18): 48=18×2+12; 18=12×1+6; 12=6×2+0 → HCF=6

LCM (Lowest Common Multiple):
The smallest number that is divisible by two or more numbers.

METHODS TO FIND LCM:
1. Prime Factorisation: LCM = product of ALL prime factors with HIGHEST powers.
   Example: 12=2²×3, 18=2×3². LCM = 2²×3² = 4×9 = 36

2. Division Method: Divide all numbers by a common factor repeatedly until all become 1.

KEY RELATIONSHIP:
HCF × LCM = Product of the two numbers
For numbers a and b: HCF(a,b) × LCM(a,b) = a × b

APPLICATIONS:
- Largest tile/plank: HCF of dimensions
- Bells ringing together: LCM of intervals
- Minimum distance/quantity: LCM
- Distributing items equally: HCF
points: HCF = product of COMMON factors with LOWEST powers.
LCM = product of ALL factors with HIGHEST powers.
HCF × LCM = Product of the two numbers.
Euclidean Algorithm for HCF: divide repeatedly until remainder = 0.
HCF ≤ smaller number; LCM ≥ larger number.
If HCF of two numbers = 1, they are co-prime.
HCF divides both numbers exactly; LCM is divisible by both.
For 3 numbers: LCM × HCF ≠ product (relation doesn't extend simply).
Tile problem: largest square tile for a room → HCF of length and breadth.
Bells: ring together after LCM of their individual intervals.
examples: Largest tile for 12m×8m room: HCF(12,8)=4m
Bells ring at 6,8,12 minute intervals. Ring together after LCM(6,8,12)=24 minutes
HCF(17,19)=1 → they are co-prime (both prime numbers)
alg-1.summary: HCF = highest factor common to all numbers (use lowest powers of common primes). LCM = lowest multiple common to all numbers (use highest powers of all primes). Key formula: HCF × LCM = product of two numbers. Application: HCF for dividing/tiling, LCM for synchronisation/minimum quantity. Euclidean algorithm finds HCF efficiently.

alg-2.title: Ratio, Proportion and Variation
alg-2.notes:
Ratio, proportion, and variation are fundamental algebraic tools applied in speed, work, mixture, and geometry problems.

RATIO:
A ratio a:b compares two quantities of the same kind.
a:b = a/b
Equivalent ratios: a:b = ka:kb for any k≠0
To compare ratios, convert to fractions.

PROPORTION:
Four quantities a, b, c, d are in proportion if a:b = c:d, written a:b::c:d.
Cross-multiplication: a×d = b×c (product of extremes = product of means)
Mean proportional of a and b: x where a:x = x:b → x² = ab → x = √(ab)
Third proportional to a and b: x where a:b = b:x → x = b²/a

TYPES:
Direct Proportion: y ∝ x → y = kx. As x increases, y increases.
Inverse Proportion: y ∝ 1/x → xy = k. As x increases, y decreases.

COMPOUND RATIO: a:b and c:d → Compound ratio = ac:bd
DUPLICATE RATIO: a:b → a²:b²
SUB-DUPLICATE RATIO: a:b → √a:√b
TRIPLICATE RATIO: a:b → a³:b³

VARIATION:
Joint variation: z ∝ xy → z = kxy
Partial variation: z = kx + c

KEY APPLICATIONS:
If A:B = 3:4 and B:C = 5:6, find A:C:
A:C = (3×5):(4×6) = 15:24 = 5:8

MIXTURES:
If 2 solutions are mixed, weighted average: (C₁V₁ + C₂V₂)/(V₁+V₂)
points: a:b::c:d means product of extremes = product of means: ad=bc.
Mean proportional of a and b = √(ab).
Direct proportion: y=kx (same direction change).
Inverse proportion: xy=k (opposite direction change).
Duplicate ratio of a:b is a²:b²; sub-duplicate is √a:√b.
Compound ratio of a:b and c:d is ac:bd.
To compare a:b and c:d, cross multiply: ad vs bc.
If A:B=m:n and B:C=p:q then A:C=mp:nq.
Componendo: a/b=c/d → (a+b)/b=(c+d)/d.
Dividendo: a/b=c/d → (a−b)/b=(c−d)/d.
examples: Mean proportional of 4 and 9 = √(4×9)=√36=6
If 5 workers do a job in 8 days, 10 workers (inverse): 5×8=10×d → d=4 days
Compound ratio of 2:3 and 4:5 = 8:15
alg-2.summary: Ratio a:b = a/b. Proportion a:b::c:d → ad=bc. Mean proportional = √(ab). Direct proportion: y=kx; inverse: xy=k. Duplicate ratio: a²:b²; compound ratio of a:b and c:d is ac:bd. To combine ratios A:B and B:C → A:C = (A×B's multiplied):(B×C's multiplied). Componendo-dividendo are useful shortcuts.
